subject.title: Self-host: local console sign-in without Cloudflare Access (follow-up to #95 / #104)

question: Should ClawRouter support an opt-in local cookie-session login for the self-host profile, using the existing admin token while refusing activation on Cloudflare Access deployments?
rationale: This is a new core authentication mode rather than a repair to an established contract, and it changes the supported security and operator model for self-hosted deployments.

options.title: Approve the opt-in local-session direction
options.body: Review and, if security details hold, merge the linked PR while retaining the API-only default and refusing mixed Access/local-auth configuration.

options.title: Keep self-host API-only
options.body: Decline browser-console sessions for the supported self-host profile and retain bearer-token administration as the documented boundary.

options.title: Request a narrower follow-up design
options.body: Require a revised proposal that defines a different supported local identity or deployment-security model before accepting browser sessions.

recommendation.title: Approve the opt-in local-session direction
recommendation.body: Review and, if security details hold, merge the linked PR while retaining the API-only default and refusing mixed Access/local-auth configuration.

likelyOwner.reason: The merged self-host baseline and adjacent session features provide the strongest available repository-history connection to this product boundary.
